summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 13 streaming replication across node1 (initial primary), node2 and node3 (standbys) on RHEL 9. Opened firewalld port 5432 on all nodes, created a scram-sha-256 replicator role, and built standbys via pg_basebackup -R. Verified healthy async streaming replication and committed-data propagation. Simulated primary loss by stopping PostgreSQL on node1, promoted node2 to writable primary via pg_ctl promote with zero data loss (all pre-failover committed rows present, new writes accepted), repointed node3 to stream from node2, and rebuilt node1 as a standby of node2 via fresh pg_basebackup. Confirmed live writes on node2 replicate to both node1 and node3. Then ran the mandatory node-restart protocol: for each of node1, node3, and node2 (in that order, one at a time, preserving quorum), captured a pre-restart boot_id and health baseline, triggered systemctl reboot with an async wrapper so the ack returned before disconnection, polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed, and verified PostgreSQL/replication/data fully recovered after each restart (node2 came back as the writable primary with all data intact and both standbys reconnected).
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server 13.23 on node1, node2, node3
Opened firewalld port 5432/tcp on all three nodes
Initialized primary DB on node1, configured wal_level=replica, hot_standby, pg_hba.conf for replication and app connections
Created replicator role with scram-sha-256 password (generated on node1, passed via secret_env)
Built node2 and node3 as standbys of node1 via pg_basebackup -R
Verified streaming replication healthy and appdb test table replicated to both standbys
Inserted pre-failover committed row and confirmed presence on both standbys before disruption
Stopped postgresql on node1 to simulate primary loss (quorum of 2 standbys preserved)
Promoted node2 to writable primary via pg_ctl promote; verified no data loss and new writes accepted
Repointed node3's primary_conninfo to node2 and confirmed it streams from the new primary with full data
Rebuilt node1 as a standby of node2 via pg_basebackup -R and cleaned up postgresql.auto.conf
Verified live write on node2 replicates to both node1 and node3

Ran mandatory node-restart protocol on node1, node3, node2 sequentially: captured boot_id + health baseline, triggered async systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, verified changed boot_id, verified PostgreSQL/replication/data recovery after each restart
Confirmed final state: node2 primary (post-restart), node1 and node3 streaming standbys, all data consistent

evidence.requirement: Initial streaming replication topology: node1 primary, node2/node3 standbys, healthy
evidence.summary: PostgreSQL initialized on node1 with replication role; node2 and node3 built via pg_basebackup -R and started; pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both standbys streaming; both standbys show pg_is_in_recovery=t and replicated baseline row

evidence.requirement: Pre-failover committed data reaches standbys before disruption
evidence.summary: Inserted 'pre-failover-committed' row on node1 primary; confirmed present on node2 and node3 via matching WAL replay LSN before primary was stopped

evidence.requirement: Primary loss simulated with quorum preserved (one node disrupted, two remain)
evidence.summary: systemctl stop postgresql on node1 confirmed inactive, while node2 and node3 remained running standbys

evidence.requirement: Standby promotion to writable primary without losing committed data
evidence.summary: pg_ctl promote on node2 succeeded (pg_is_in_recovery=f); appdb table shows pre-failover-committed row intact plus successful new write post-promotion

evidence.requirement: Third node repointed to new primary and recovered former primary rejoined as standby of new primary
evidence.summary: node3 primary_conninfo repointed to node2, confirmed streaming with full data; node1 rebuilt via pg_basebackup from node2 and restarted as standby (pg_is_in_recovery=t) with all data including post-failover write; node2 pg_stat_replication shows both node1 and node3 streaming

evidence.requirement: End-to-end replication continues correctly after recovery
evidence.summary: New write on node2 (post-recovery-check) propagated to both node1 and node3

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id fbdf5b2c captured with postgresql active and pg_is_in_recovery=t; reboot acknowledged async; node unreachable then reachable again; new boot_id d9b12230 (changed); post-restart standby recovered with full data and reappeared in node2's pg_stat_replication

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bf4e9cbb captured with active postgresql and 4-row dataset; reboot acknowledged async; node unreachable then reachable; new boot_id 6139659a (changed); standby recovered with full data and reappeared streaming on node2

evidence.requirement: node2 (primary) restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state as primary with quorum restored
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 6bb7e004 captured with postgresql active as primary (pg_is_in_recovery=f); reboot acknowledged async; node unreachable then reachable; new boot_id 90b24959 (changed); node2 resumed as writable primary with all data intact, both standbys reconnected, and a fresh write successfully replicated to both node1 and node3
